Senses.Explanation: Ordinary mind in the Chan record is not a special state to be approached or captured by a stock rule. Mazu Daoyi supplies the fullest direct description: after saying that the Way does not need refining but must not be defiled, he says “ordinary mind is the Way” (平常心是道) and answers “what is ordinary mind?” with “no contriving, no right-and-wrong, no grasping-or-rejecting, no annihilation-or-permanence, no ordinary-or-holy” (無造作、無是非、無取捨、無斷常、無凡聖). In the Nanquan Puyuan and Zhaozhou Congshen dialogue, Nanquan again says “ordinary mind is the Way”; when Zhaozhou asks whether one can head toward it or know it without heading toward it, Nanquan says that aiming is already off and that the Way belongs neither to knowing nor not knowing. Other public answers name unremarkable responses and creatures: Changsha Jingcen says “when you want to sleep, sleep; when you want to sit, sit,” then “hot, take the cool; cold, go to the fire”; Zhaozhou says “foxes, wolves, and jackals are it”; Xianglin Chengyuan says “at dawn, the morning greeting; in the evening, take care.” Zhenjing Kewen in turn rebukes making “ordinary mind is the Way” into a final rule. These answers and restrictions concern one ordinary mind; the larger sentence is evidence about the headword, not a second lexical thing.
Senses.Note: Allowlist count: 309 hits in 120 texts. The sentence “ordinary mind is the Way” (平常心是道) occurs 181 times in 100 texts, and the question “what is ordinary mind?” (如何是平常心) occurs 30 times in 19. Zhenjing Kewen warns against taking the sentence as an ultimate rule; that criticism narrows the same referent and does not create another sense. Item-8 readjudication therefore keeps one corpus-wide sense. Related family entries for the Way (道), “mind itself is buddha” (即心是佛), and “without contriving” (無造作) remain compatible with this description.

Occurrences.Kwic: 道不用修，但莫污染。何為污染？但有生死心，造作趣向，皆是染污。若欲直會其道，平常心是道。何謂平常心？無造作、無是非、無取捨，無斷常、無凡聖。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Tiansheng Expanded Lamp Record (天聖廣燈錄), section on Jiangxi Mazu Daji. Mazu Daoyi addresses the assembly, says that ordinary mind is the Way, and directly answers what ordinary mind is; the preceding Baizhang exchange closes before this address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州問南泉：如何是道？泉云：平常心是道。州云：還可趣向也無？泉云：擬趣即乖。州云：不擬爭知是道？泉云：道不屬知，不屬不知。知是妄覺，不知是無記。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Essentials of the Old Worthies (續古尊宿語要), an old case raised inside a later address. Zhaozhou Congshen asks the questions, while Nanquan Puyuan owns the exact headword turn and says that aiming toward it is already off.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州問南泉：「如何是道？」泉云：「平常心是道。」州云：「還可趨向不？」泉云：「擬即乖。」州云：「不擬怎知是道？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jiguang Huo (寂光豁禪師語錄), verse-commentary section quoting the old case. Zhaozhou Congshen asks how one can know, while Nanquan Puyuan owns the exact headword answer; Jiguang Huo is the later recorder, not either case speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是平常心？師曰：要眠即眠，要坐即坐。曰：學人不會，意旨如何？師曰：熱即取涼，寒即向火。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Succession of Five Lamps, fascicles 1–9 (五燈嚴統(第1卷-第9卷)), section on Changsha Jingcen. An unnamed questioner asks what ordinary mind is; Changsha owns both answers about sleeping, sitting, cooling, and warming.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「如何是平常心？」師云：「狐狼野干是。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Venerable Zhaozhou (趙州和尚語錄), Zhaozhou Congshen's own encounter record. An unnamed questioner asks what ordinary mind is, and Zhaozhou answers that foxes, wolves, and jackals are it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是平常心。師曰。早朝不審。晚後珍重。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Xianglin Chengyuan. An unnamed questioner asks what ordinary mind is, and Xianglin answers with the morning greeting and evening farewell; the section remains in Xianglin's voice.

Occurrences.Kwic: 或又報箇平常心是道，以為極則，天是天、地是地、山是山、水是水、僧是僧、俗是俗
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jiatai Universal Lamp Record (嘉泰普燈錄), section on Letan Zhenjing Kewen. Zhenjing Kewen addresses the assembly and rebukes reporting “ordinary mind is the Way” as the final rule; this is his own criticism, not an anonymous compiler's gloss.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。若欲求佛即心是佛。若欲會道無心是道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), section on Sikong Benjing. Imperial envoy Yang Guangting asks about buddha and the Way; Sikong Benjing answers “if you seek buddha, mind itself is buddha.” This anchors the related phrase and does not count toward headword depth.
